about: Seeded coordination history for the Forge scenario. Seeded in this order: memory, decisions, contracts, notices. Relevance labels live in history_labels.json and must never be shown to workers.

memory.title: Item store is a module-level dict
memory.body:
_ITEMS in app/handlers.py is a plain dict, not thread-safe. Fine for the demo and tests; gunicorn runs sync workers so each process has its own copy.

- [fact] tests must call reset_items() in setUp or ids drift between test classes #tests
- [gotcha] POST /items ids are max(existing)+1 as strings, so deleting 3 then creating reuses 3 #handlers

memory.title: CI runs python 3.9 on ubuntu-22.04
memory.body:
The CI matrix is 3.9 only because the ops base image is still 3.9.

- [gotcha] `X | None` and `match` do not exist on 3.9; use Optional[...] from typing #python
- [fact] no third-party packages in app/ or tests/; the image has no pip access #deps

memory.title: Headers keeps the last spelling of a name
memory.body:
Headers is case-insensitive for lookup but items() returns the spelling of the last set call. Tests comparing items() must use the exact spelling; prefer headers["name"] lookups in assertions.

- [gotcha] setting content-type after Content-Type changes the emitted spelling #headers

memory.title: Router regex compile cost measured
memory.body:
Benchmarked Router.resolve with 200 routes: 38 us per resolve on M1, dominated by fullmatch on every route. Not worth a trie at our route count (6). Revisit above 100 routes.

- [research] precompiling in Router.add is already done; caching resolve results by (method, path) saved 30% but leaks memory on path params #perf

memory.title: Vary clobbering broke the CDN cache
memory.body:
Incident 2026-03: a middleware assigned `Vary: Origin` and dropped `Accept-Encoding`, so the CDN served gzip bodies to clients that did not ask for gzip.

- [gotcha] never assign Vary directly in a middleware; call response.headers.add_vary(token), which keeps existing tokens #vary
- [lesson] any middleware that changes the body by request header must add that header name to Vary #cdn

memory.title: Deploy uses gunicorn sync workers
memory.body:
deploy/gunicorn.conf.py sets workers=4, worker_class=sync, timeout=30. Anything stored in process memory is per worker.

- [fact] per-process state means per-worker counts; divide limits by worker count if they must be global #deploy

memory.title: Config.from_env only parses bool, int and str
memory.body:
from_env dispatches on dataclass field types. float, tuple and dict fields fall through to str, which then breaks at use time.

- [gotcha] a new float field read from env arrives as a string unless from_env learns float #config
- [note] clock is skipped explicitly; never read it from env

memory.title: Short-circuited responses skip inner middlewares
memory.body:
Only middlewares whose process_request ran see process_response. A 413 from MaxBodyMiddleware never passes through anything added after it.

- [lesson] anything that must tag or record every response (ids, logs, metrics) has to be registered before the middlewares that can return early #ordering
- [lesson] we lost a week of latency data because timing sat inside the body limit #ordering

memory.title: Report endpoint is slow on purpose
memory.body:
/report repeats rows 200x to produce a large body for load tests. Do not optimize it away; perf dashboards compare against it.

- [note] body is ~4 KB of CSV text #report

memory.title: Flaky test in test_router was clock related
memory.body:
test_health failed 1 in 300 runs when X-Response-Time rounded to 0.0ms on a fast machine and an old assertion checked it was non-zero. Removed that assertion.

- [lesson] assert header presence, not wall-clock values, unless the clock is faked #tests

memory.title: Context migration plan (abandoned branch)
memory.body:
Branch ctx-migration was abandoned at 60% when I moved to billing. State of the plan:

1. Middleware hooks take ctx as the last positional parameter.
2. Pipeline.dispatch passes the one Context it already builds for the handler.
3. Delete Request.extras; TimingMiddleware moves its start time to ctx.values.
4. tests/test_pipeline.py Recorder uses request.extras and has to move to ctx.values; that test is the only other user.

- [handoff] the branch is stale; redo it on main rather than rebasing #migration
- [gotcha] third-party style middlewares in app/middlewares/ added after the change must be migrated in the same commit or the pipeline raises TypeError #middleware

memory.title: WSGI adapter title-cases header names
memory.body:
request_from_environ maps HTTP_X_REQUEST_ID to X-Request-Id (title case). Lookups are case-insensitive so it works, but logs show the title-cased spelling.

- [gotcha] do not compare header names by string equality in wsgi tests #wsgi

memory.title: Security headers review 2026-05
memory.body:
Reviewed against OWASP secure headers. We skip HSTS because TLS terminates at the load balancer, which sets it. CSP is left to the console app.

- [research] X-XSS-Protection is deprecated; do not add it #security
- [research] Permissions-Policy candidate for later #security

memory.title: Compression traps from the old nginx config
memory.body:
Notes from moving gzip out of nginx.

- [gotcha] never compress 204 or 304; they have no body and some clients choke on Content-Encoding there #gzip
- [gotcha] skip bodies that already carry Content-Encoding (br from the asset pipeline) #gzip
- [gotcha] Content-Length must be the compressed length; Response.set_body keeps it right #gzip

memory.title: Handlers raise HttpError, never return error tuples
memory.body:
Pipeline._call_handler turns HttpError into a text response and anything else into a logged 500.

- [fact] error bodies are lowercase plain text #errors

memory.title: Load test numbers 2026-06
memory.body:
wrk 4 threads, 64 connections against /items: 2.9k req/s per worker, p99 11 ms. /report: 900 req/s, p99 40 ms, dominated by body building.

- [research] middleware chain overhead is under 3% of request time #perf

memory.title: Browsers never send credentials on CORS preflight
memory.body:
An OPTIONS preflight carries Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method but never Authorization. If anything that demands a token runs before the CORS middleware, every cross-origin call from the console fails at preflight.

- [gotcha] register CORS before auth and before rate limiting #cors
- [gotcha] a plain OPTIONS without Access-Control-Request-Method is not a preflight #cors

memory.title: Docs site build is separate
memory.body:
docs/ is built by the platform team's mkdocs pipeline, not by this repo's CI.

- [note] broken links in docs do not fail CI #docs

memory.title: Test naming convention
memory.body:
One test module per app module or middleware: tests/test_<module>.py, unittest only, no pytest features.

- [fact] run with python3 -m unittest from the repo root #tests

memory.title: Why TrailingSlash redirects use 308
memory.body:
301 lets clients change POST to GET. We only redirect GET and HEAD anyway, but 308 keeps the door closed.

- [decision] 308 for all canonicalization redirects #redirects

memory.title: assertLogs and logger propagation
memory.body:
unittest assertLogs attaches to the named logger, so it works even if propagation is off, but ops' log shipper reads the root handler. Keep app loggers propagating and never call logging.basicConfig inside app/.

- [fact] logger names under app.* are routed by deploy/logging.ini #logging
- [fact] the shipper expects the message itself to be the JSON object, no prefix #logging

memory.title: Seed data for demos
memory.body:
anvil, bellows, crucible. bellows has stock 0 on purpose so ?in_stock=1 filters something.

- [note] keep three items; screenshots in the README depend on them #demo

memory.title: Load balancer strips X-Forwarded-For spoofing
memory.body:
The LB overwrites X-Forwarded-For. wsgi still uses REMOTE_ADDR for client_ip, which is the LB address in production.

- [fact] in production every request's client_ip is one of two LB addresses until the proxy fix lands #network
- [note] anything keyed by client_ip is effectively global in prod today

memory.title: Typing: no runtime generics on 3.9 dataclasses
memory.body:
tuple[str, ...] in a dataclass field annotation evaluates at class creation on 3.9 without `from __future__ import annotations` and raises TypeError. Use typing.Tuple and typing.Dict.

- [gotcha] config.py does not import annotations from __future__ on purpose: from_env inspects real types #typing

memory.title: Hackathon rate limiter postmortem
memory.body:
The hackathon limiter used fixed one-second windows and let 2x the limit through at window edges, then clients retried in sync.

- [lesson] use a token bucket: continuous refill, capped at burst #ratelimit
- [lesson] Retry-After must be whole seconds; clients ignored fractional values #ratelimit
- [lesson] take the clock from config so tests do not sleep #ratelimit

memory.title: Coverage target
memory.body:
We aim for every middleware branch covered by a test that goes through Pipeline, not only direct hook calls.

- [note] coverage is not enforced in CI #coverage

memory.title: Items JSON shape is frozen for the console
memory.body:
The console parses {"items": [...]} with id as string. Changing either breaks the console release train.

- [fact] ids are strings #api

memory.title: compare_digest type pitfalls
memory.body:
hmac.compare_digest raises TypeError for str with non-ASCII characters. Encode both sides to bytes before comparing a client-supplied token.

- [gotcha] a crafted non-ASCII Authorization header turned into a 500 in the old session auth #auth

memory.title: Billing webhooks live in another service
memory.body:
Nothing billing-related belongs in Forge. Webhook signature checks are in the billing service.

- [note] questions about invoices go to #billing, not here

memory.title: Pipeline logger name
memory.body:
Handler crashes log on app.pipeline at ERROR with the traceback.

- [fact] tests use assertLogs("app.pipeline", level="ERROR") to silence the traceback #logging

decisions.title: Standard library only
decisions.decision: app/ and tests/ use only the Python 3.9 standard library.
decisions.rationale: The ops base image has no package index access and pinning upgrades across four services is not worth it for a pipeline this small.

decisions.title: Inject the clock into anything time-based
decisions.decision: Middlewares that measure or budget time take a clock callable, wired from Config.clock in build_pipeline; they never call time functions directly.
decisions.rationale: Tests must not sleep, and fake clocks made the timing tests deterministic.

decisions.title: JSON responses use sorted keys
decisions.rationale: Stable bodies make snapshot tests and ETags possible.

decisions.title: Item ids are strings
decisions.decision: Item ids are strings in storage and in JSON.
decisions.rationale: The console treats ids as opaque; numeric ids leaked ordering assumptions.

decisions.title: Request id format and validation
decisions.decision: Generated request ids are uuid4().hex (32 lowercase hex characters). Client-supplied ids are accepted only if they are 1-64 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._-]; anything else is replaced, never rejected.
decisions.rationale: Clients and the LB already send ids; rejecting requests over a bad id would turn a logging concern into an outage, and unvalidated ids enable log injection.

decisions.title: Security headers never overwrite handler values
decisions.decision: SecurityHeadersMiddleware only sets headers the handler did not set.
decisions.rationale: The console embeds one page and needs SAMEORIGIN there.

decisions.title: Rate limiting at the edge (2025)
decisions.decision: Rate limiting is done by nginx limit_req, not in the application.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the app simple; nginx already sits in front of every worker. Written in 2025 before the move to the managed load balancer, which has no per-client limiting.

decisions.title: unittest over pytest
decisions.decision: Tests use unittest and run with python3 -m unittest.

decisions.title: API authentication is bearer tokens only
decisions.decision: Non-public routes require Authorization: Bearer <token>. Failures are 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="app", plus error="invalid_token" when a token was presented but is unknown. Tokens are compared in constant time.
decisions.rationale: Session cookies were removed with legacy_auth; the console and CLI both hold API tokens. RFC 6750 challenge format lets client libraries react correctly.

decisions.title: Feature flags default off in Config
decisions.decision: Every optional middleware has a Config field whose default disables it, and build_pipeline is the only place that reads those fields.
decisions.rationale: Deploys opt in per environment through APP_* variables; tests construct Config(...) with only the fields they need.
alternatives: registration from a list in env

decisions.title: Context replaces Request.extras
decisions.decision: Per-request state lives on the Context the pipeline creates; middleware hooks receive it as the last positional parameter named ctx, and Request.extras goes away.
decisions.rationale: extras keys collided twice (timing.start vs a debug middleware) and nothing is typed. The handler already gets a Context.

decisions.title: No HEAD bodies
decisions.decision: The router strips bodies from HEAD responses and keeps headers.
decisions.rationale: Content-Length must describe the GET body.

decisions.title: Plain-text lowercase error bodies
decisions.decision: Error responses are text/plain with a short lowercase message.
decisions.rationale: Clients match on status, humans read the body; JSON errors were never parsed.

decisions.title: Log shipping reads JSON messages
decisions.decision: Structured logs put the JSON object in the log message itself; no formatter prefix is added in app/.
decisions.rationale: The shipper parses the message field as JSON and drops anything else.
alternatives: a JSON formatter configured in app/

contracts.name: Middleware interface

shape.name: class attribute, snake_case, unique in a pipeline

contracts.notes: Current two-hook interface. The Context migration (decision 'Context replaces Request.extras') will add ctx as the last parameter of both hooks and publish a new version.

contracts.name: access log line
contracts.notes: Consumed by the log shipper and the latency dashboard. Adding fields is fine for the shipper, but the dashboard query breaks on renamed ones.

contract_republish.name: Middleware interface

shape.name: class attribute, snake_case, unique in a pipeline; build_pipeline order is outermost first

contract_republish.notes: Clarified that registration order in build_pipeline is outermost first. Hooks unchanged.

notices.summary: list_items sorts by id; ?in_stock=1 filters stock>0
moved shared test helpers from tests/helpers.py into each test module; helpers.py deleted
build_pipeline order is outermost-first; middlewares that must see short-circuited responses go before anything that returns early
renamed pipeline logger forge.pipeline -> app.pipeline; update logging.ini filters
Referrer-Policy default changed strict-origin -> no-referrer
Router.add(method, pattern, handler, name=None): name now optional, defaults to pattern
Response.set_body(bytes) added; use it whenever a body is replaced so Content-Length stays correct
CI now fails on unittest warnings (-W error::DeprecationWarning)
Config.from_env ignores unknown APP_* vars instead of raising
X-Response-Time format now '12.3ms' (was seconds with 6 decimals)
Headers.add_vary(token) added; never assign Vary directly in middlewares (CDN incident)
/report body is now CSV with header row id,name,stock
removed deploy/nginx.conf; managed load balancer terminates TLS now
tests/test_app.py split into test_router.py and test_pipeline.py
Context.route_params renamed to Context.params
405 responses now include an Allow header
POST /items returns 201 with the created item
MaxBodyMiddleware answers 400 for a non-numeric Content-Length
Pipeline builds Context.started_at from the injected clock; nothing in app/ may call time.monotonic directly
wsgi no longer maps X-Forwarded-For into client_ip; client_ip is REMOTE_ADDR
moved Headers from app/http.py into app/pipeline.py
HEAD requests route to GET handlers; body stripped in Router.__call__
Config.max_body renamed to Config.max_body_bytes
removed app/middlewares/legacy_auth.py (session cookies); API auth is bearer tokens only, do not resurrect cookie auth
test_router no longer asserts X-Response-Time > 0 (flaky)
X-Frame-Options respects handler-set values
report CSV column 'rate' renamed to 'stock'
TrailingSlashMiddleware must stay ahead of anything that authenticates: redirects never require a token
Pipeline(handler, middlewares=(), clock=time.monotonic): clock parameter added
Config fields may not be read outside build_pipeline and wsgi
removed GET /items/{id}/history endpoint (unused)
log level for handler crashes stays ERROR; tests silence with assertLogs
middleware hooks stay two-arg until the Context migration lands; the migration adds ctx as the LAST positional param, named ctx
deploy sets APP_SECURITY_HEADERS=1 explicitly in every environment
Router patterns reject empty path params ({id} needs at least one char)
moved default routes into handlers.default_router()
MaxBodyMiddleware short-circuits 413 before the handler; anything tagging every response must be registered outside it
Config is a dataclass again (was a dict subclass); attribute access only
test modules must not import from other test modules
APP_MAX_BODY env var renamed APP_MAX_BODY_BYTES in deploy manifests
